currentContext.business: The Company's owned businesses are Chemicals, Estate Management and Finance & Investments, with GIL Chemicals manufacturing units at Ambernath (Maharashtra), Valia (Gujarat), Kheda (Gujarat) and Kundaim (Goa). Through its business structure it holds 23.7% of Godrej Consumer Products Limited, 44.8% of Godrej Properties Limited, 65.1% of Godrej Agrovet Limited and 100% of Godrej Investment Limited (Financial Services), alongside other investments. The group therefore serves consumer, real-estate, agri-value-chain and financial-services customers, with Godrej Properties operating as India's largest residential developer by booking value and Godrej Agrovet operating across animal nutrition, crop care, oil palm, dairy, and poultry & processed foods.

currentContext.expansion: The single named project with a timeline is Godrej Agrovet's Palm Kernel Oil (PKO) refinery: work is described as progressing well and in full swing, with the facility expected to commence operations in FY 2026-27. It is positioned as a key strategic initiative to diversify the product portfolio, enhance realisations and capture a higher share of the value chain, in line with GAVL's stated commitment to further margin expansion through downstream integration and value-added opportunities. Supporting Oil Palm expansion is sustained investment across the value chain - plantation development, nursery operations and farmer engagement - including the addition of 10 new Samadhan centres during FY 2025-26 (5 of them in the North East), taking the network to 24 centres. In Chemicals, the Company has invested in building manufacturing capacities and in R&D capability, anchored by NGSTAR, an 8,000 sq. ft. technology and application research centre at the Ambernath factory, with the R&D team size more than doubling; the business also ran initiatives to improve yields, throughput and energy saving. In Crop Care, expansion is portfolio-led rather than asset-led, through new product launches and strategic entry into additional crops such as maize and paddy. On the real-estate side, Godrej Properties' growth capacity rests on a diversified and growing project pipeline spanning 15+ cities supported by a healthy balance sheet and strong liquidity. No rupee capex outlay for the Company's own businesses is disclosed in the routed text.

risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict in the Middle East and energy/commodity supply shock
risks.note: The global economy is disrupted by the outbreak of war in the Middle East, with rising commodity prices, firmer inflation expectations and tighter financial conditions. Elevated energy and other commodity prices coupled with supply shock due to disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz would act as a drag on domestic production in FY 2026-27, and West Asia tensions may disrupt energy supplies and fertiliser availability - both critical inputs for agricultural production.

risks.risk: Below-normal monsoon and climate variability hitting the agri value chain
risks.note: IMD's first-stage forecast puts monsoon rainfall at 92% of the Long Period Average (+/-5%), a likely below-normal outcome due to El Nino. With 51% of cultivated land rain-fed (about 40% of production) and nearly 47% of the population dependent on agriculture, a weaker monsoon could dampen rural consumption and push up food inflation - directly relevant to the group's animal nutrition, crop care, oil palm and dairy exposures.

risks.risk: Global financial market volatility spilling into domestic financial conditions
risks.note: Heightened volatility in global financial markets with its spillover on domestic financial conditions would weigh on growth prospects; risks to the global outlook are described as decisively on the downside, with high public debt and eroded policy buffers adding vulnerability.

Fragmented landholdings, climate pressures, irrigation constraints and rural-to-urban migration persist as structural challenges, and land fragmentation plus income uncertainty keep farm incomes volatile - a demand risk for the agri-input and allied businesses.

risks.risk: Soft external demand and slower global growth
risks.note: The World Economic Outlook projects global growth at 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027, below recent outcomes and well under pre-pandemic averages; net external demand for India remained soft, with a prolonged conflict, deeper geopolitical fragmentation or renewed trade tensions cited as downside triggers.

risks.risk: Enterprise risk spectrum covered by the Board's Risk Management Policy
risks.note: The Board-framed Risk Management Policy identifies and assesses operational, strategic, financial, security, property, regulatory, reputational, cyber security and other risks, with a risk management infrastructure maintained to address them.

risks.risk: Evolving gaps in Internal Financial Controls as the business changes
risks.note: The Board acknowledges that IFC are not static and will evolve as the business, technology and even the fraud environment change in response to competition, industry practices, legislation, regulation and economic conditions, so gaps may arise; a process is in place to continuously identify such gaps and implement improved controls.

risks.risk: Rising regulatory and compliance burden in financial services
risks.note: The regulatory environment remains focused on financial stability, transparency and consumer protection; while evolving regulations reinforce systemic resilience, they necessitate higher compliance and governance standards for the group's growing lending and wealth/asset management platform.
